entities.name: The Modern Prison (Penitentiary System)
entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: Eastern State Penitentiary (Philadelphia, 1829) pioneered solitary confinement as rehabilitation — prisoners lived alone in cells, reflecting on their sins (hence "penitentiary"). The Auburn System (New York) used silent group labor by day and solitary cells by night. Both systems drove many prisoners insane.
